PullRequest.Title: Preserve draft agent selections across host materialization
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Follow-up to #344955 for the remaining Agents Window draft issue from #318422: one client agent appeared twice after host materialization, and picking its original file URI could lose the selection on the first message.

- Correlate client draft files with advertised host agents using the validated optional `vscode.sourceUri` provenance and the existing bundle source map. Prefer the host-backed entry without collapsing different definitions that share a name.
- Reconcile selections when host customizations arrive, when a draft source is picked, and before the first send. Wait while the selected source's enabled customization is loading; report a loading failure rather than dispatching with the default agent.
- Resolve remembered draft-source selections through an optional provider API. Host-advertised URIs remain authoritative; no cache-path guessing, authored-name matching, new wire metadata, SDK identity changes, or host-side metadata reading.
- Preserve existing behavior for absent, malformed, case-distinct, or ambiguous provenance and for hosts that do not implement optional resolution.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- Focused provider and picker suites — **597 passed, 11 pre-existing pending/platform skips**; no new skips:

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\agentHost\test\browser\localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\agentHost\test\browser\agentHostAgentPicker.test.ts --reporter dot
```

- Changed TypeScript hygiene, including formatting and ESLint — **5 files passed**:

```powershell
node build\hygiene.ts src\vs\sessions\common\agentHostSessionsProvider.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\agentHost\browser\baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\agentHost\browser\agentHostAgentPicker.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\agentHost\test\browser\localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts src\vs\sessions\contrib\providers\agentHost\test\browser\agentHostAgentPicker.test.ts
```

- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

Regression coverage includes simultaneous client/host copies, distinct same-named sources, opaque non-VS-Code host URIs, bundle translation, invalid/missing/ambiguous/case-distinct metadata, remembered selections, delayed host loading, clearing a selection while waiting, first-send/graduation identity, and load errors without dispatch.

### Live Code OSS verification

Verified on Windows with dbgjs attached to the renderer and agent host. A fresh draft showed exactly three `Reviewer` definitions with their extension/plugin captions instead of six rows. Original client-file selections were translated to host-advertised URIs before sending. Fresh extension and plugin selections produced `EXTENSION-REVIEWER` and `PLUGIN-REVIEWER` respectively on their first turn, and the picker remained on `Reviewer` after graduation.

Full smoke/E2E suites, macOS/Linux live UI flows, and a physical screen-reader check were not run.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The nested loop, synchronous UI call path, and shared inventory sources are directly established in code. Exact user inventory sizes vary, which affects severity, but not the quadratic mechanism or its reachability.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Renderer CPU and temporary URI/metadata objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For C client-discovered agents and P host-published agents, getCustomAgents now performs Θ(C×P) candidate comparisons (an exact find plus a full provenance filter per client agent); after materialization C and P commonly describe the same inventory, making this quadratic.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Synchronous picker/catalog refreshes take increasing CPU time and allocation/GC pressure, delaying agent-picker updates or opening/switching a draft in large customization inventories.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The draft merge built one map of published URIs and inserted each client agent once, so the merge was linear in C+P apart from the final sort.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each client agent now calls _resolvePublishedDraftAgent, which scans the complete published array for an exact URI and, when the host URI differs as intended here, scans it again while allocating validated metadata views and parsing provenance URIs.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 7200 adds _resolvePublishedDraftAgent inside the loop over every client agent; that helper scans all published agents, replacing the prior direct ResourceMap insertion path.
Findings.Title: Index published provenance before merging draft agents
Findings.Impact: When a workspace/profile/extensions/plugins contribute many agent files and the host advertises their materialized copies, every synchronous getCustomAgents refresh from active-session or customization changes can perform a quadratic number of URI parses/comparisons, causing visible picker latency and renderer CPU/GC spikes.
Findings.Evidence: AgentCustomizationScope populates clientAgents from every eligible local, user, extension, and plugin agent file (resolveLocalCustomAgents), while getEffectiveAgents returns the host-published counterparts. AgentHostAgentPicker._initAgent calls getCustomAgents synchronously on active-session/mode changes and onDidChangeCustomAgents. At the changed loop, every client entry calls _resolvePublishedDraftAgent; lines 7208-7218 use published.find followed by published.filter, and readAgentCustomizationMeta allocates a result object and validates/parses sourceUri for each candidate.
Findings.Recommendation: Build exact-URI and source-URI indexes from published once per getCustomAgents call (retaining an explicit ambiguous-source state), then resolve every client agent in O(1); reuse the same indexed snapshot for resolveCustomAgent where possible.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch to a draft Agents session and refresh its custom-agent picker after client/host customization discovery
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The active-session/picker autorun synchronously calls provider.getCustomAgents before the picker can reflect the catalog. Client discovery and host publication have already completed; the changed nested reconciliation itself is on the renderer critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Enumerate and read eligible agent files to build the client custom-agent snapshot
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One read per eligible agent file, scheduled concurrently after deduplicated enumeration
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same discovery reads populated client agents before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Upstream asynchronous discovery must finish before its snapshot changes, but these reads are not added by this diff; the reported regression is the subsequent synchronous merge.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Receive subscribed agent-host SessionState containing published customizations
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One already-established state update stream per draft session; updates are not per agent
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same subscription delivered host customizations, followed by a linear URI-map merge.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Provides the published snapshot and triggers a catalog refresh; the diff does not add an IPC request, but adds quadratic local work after the update.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: C eligible client agent files discovered across local, user, extension, and plugin sources and P effective host-published agents after deduplication. Materialized sessions commonly have C≈P; the changed merge performs Θ(C×P) comparisons rather than the previous linear merge, plus sorting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The picker/catalog computation is synchronous and unbounded on one renderer turn. Upstream discovery is debounced by 50 ms and performs file reads concurrently, but that does not limit or parallelize the changed reconciliation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Client and host arrays are already materialized snapshots. getCustomAgents does not cache a provenance index, so every active-session/mode/custom-agent refresh rebuilds maps, reparses URIs, and repeats the cross-product. No cold/warm distinction bounds the changed CPU work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the nested client loop and two published-array scans are explicit, and synchronous picker listeners directly call getCustomAgents.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical inventories may be small, but monorepos/profiles with many workspace, user, extension, and plugin agent files make both sides large. Exact milliseconds are unmeasured, so severity is medium rather than high.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium regression: a previously linear synchronous merge is now quadratic in realistic customization inventory size.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a remembered draft-source selection when a draft becomes active or agents are advertised
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentHostAgentPicker._initAgent reads the stored URI, synchronously gets the agent catalog, canonicalizes selected/stored URIs through resolveCustomAgent, and may call setAgent before the picker state settles.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The effective published agent count P, plus the client/published catalog sizes used by getCustomAgents. There are at most two canonicalization requests per initialization, after deduplicated agent publication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All resolution is synchronous on the renderer autorun; no queue, limiter, or asynchronous boundary is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Profile storage is read through the existing storage service. resolveCustomAgent recomputes and sorts getEffectiveAgents for each nonempty URI rather than sharing the getCustomAgents snapshot, but this adds only a constant number of extra O(P log P) passes and was treated as supporting amplification rather than a separate finding.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the synchronous repeated computation; lower for material standalone impact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The extra canonicalization passes are measurable by collection size but, independently of the reported quadratic merge, are unlikely to create material user-visible cost for ordinary catalogs.
Scenarios.Verdict: Covered by the reported catalog-scaling mechanism; no separate finding to avoid duplicating the same picker refresh cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send the first message from a draft while its selected client agent's plugin is materializing
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the pre-existing configuration-ready and eager-session waits, the new wait observes in-memory backend state until the selected source's enabled plugin leaves Loading, reconciles the selection, checks for Error, then proceeds to the existing chat send boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing eager backend session creation and SessionState subscription
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One eager session/subscription per draft, shared by the wait
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The draft already eagerly created/subscribed to the backend, but send did not wait for selected-agent materialization.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Host materialization state gates the first send when the selected plugin is still loading. The diff observes this existing stream rather than issuing a new request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch the first chat request through the agent-host connection
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One send after gating, not per agent/customization
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The request was dispatched immediately after existing configuration/eager-create readiness, potentially with the draft URI/default agent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This existing boundary remains the final critical-path operation; the diff delays it only while the selected plugin is actively Loading.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Client-agent count C and top-level customization count K are scanned on each relevant mode/backend-state invalidation while the send is pending. Effective cardinalities are deduplicated snapshots for one draft, not per repository item or per message history item.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One wait/autorun per in-progress first send; it coalesces progress through observable invalidations and is disposed on success or draft cancellation. The eventual send retains its existing connection scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The wait reads already-cached client agents and SessionState customizations. It neither creates a new cache nor retries filesystem/network discovery. Warm/cold host loading changes wait duration but not boundary-call count.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: wait lifecycle, cancellation, state invalidations, and subsequent send path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Plugin loading duration depends on host and customization, but waiting is explicitly scoped to the selected source and required for the intended identity semantics. State-scan CPU is linear and typically small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression: the added latency is an intentional selected-plugin readiness dependency, introduces no new expensive boundary, and uses bounded in-memory scans.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reconcile a selected draft agent when client customizations or host SessionState customizations change
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Client observable changes and customization-changing host state updates synchronously call _reconcileNewSessionAgent before firing catalog events; only the selected agent is matched.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Upstream client customization rediscovery after prompt/plugin changes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Deduplicated eligible files, debounced by 50 ms; not initiated by reconciliation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same rediscovery updated client custom-agent snapshots and fired catalog events.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Completes before the observable callback; changed reconciliation adds only local scanning afterward.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One state-stream update per host publication change; unrelated state updates are excluded by customizationsChanged
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same state update fired customization/agent events without selected-agent provenance reconciliation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Triggers local selected-agent reconciliation before listeners; no extra IPC is generated.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: P effective published agents for one selected agent, so O(P) per qualifying update after effective-agent deduplication and sorting.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates are serialized on the renderer event/observable turn. Client discovery is 50 ms debounced; host events are filtered by customizationsChanged before reconciliation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No provenance index is cached, so the selected-agent scan repeats on qualifying updates. However, only one selected key is resolved and unrelated SessionState updates are filtered, keeping effective work bounded.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for call frequency and O(P) local work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Host/client update frequency and catalog size vary, but one selected-agent scan per filtered update is not independently severe.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: bounded per-update reconciliation is linear and not an expensive boundary fan-out.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all six changed files and the full diff. One introduced performance regression was reported: draft-to-published agent reconciliation changes a formerly linear merge into quadratic synchronous work. First-send waiting, remembered-selection resolution, customization update fanout, cache/lifecycle behavior, and transitive expensive boundaries were also traced; no other high-confidence performance issue or qualifying regression fix was found.
